$doc: Vyomi capability registry — Azure AI Search (Microsoft.Search). Proven by tests/conformance/test_capabilities.py.

azure.aisearch.query.title: Queries (BM25 keyword, vector, hybrid, semantic ranker)
limitations: Keyword ranking is Okapi BM25 (SQLite FTS5) with phrases, negation, $filter, orderby, facets and count. Vector fields are Collection(Edm.Single) scanned exactly (no HNSW graph); vectorQueries of kind vector or text (text is embedded by the field profile's vectorizer, which is the local embedding model, not the Azure OpenAI deployment it names), per-query weight, and hybrid = BM25 + vector reciprocal rank fusion (k=60). queryType semantic with a semanticConfiguration returns @search.rerankerScore (0-4), @search.captions and @search.answers, but the ranker is an approximation (embedding similarity + query-term coverage over the configured title/content fields), NOT Microsoft's L2 cross-encoder, so scores and order will differ from Azure. Suggesters (suggest + autocomplete oneTerm/twoTerms/oneTermWithContext, prefix on source field words, no fuzzy) and searchFields / searchMode=all are supported. Synonym maps and aliases are stored (CRUD) but synonyms are not applied at query time. No scoring profiles, geo or Lucene parser.

azure.aisearch.indexers.title: Data sources, indexers and skillsets (Blob, Cosmos DB, Azure SQL)
limitations: Indexers really run for azureblob (text, JSON, CSV), cosmosdb (NoSQL, from the simulated Cosmos store, optional query) and azuresql (table or view, from the simulated Azure SQL database) data sources, with fieldMappings (base64Encode/Decode, urlEncode/Decode, jsonArrayToStringCollection), outputFieldMappings, HighWaterMarkChangeDetectionPolicy (incremental, tracking state in the run status) and SoftDeleteColumnDeletionDetectionPolicy. SqlIntegratedChangeTracking, azuretable and adlsgen2 sources, managed-identity connection strings, schedules (runs are on demand) and the blob NativeBlobSoftDelete policy are not executed. Skillsets execute SplitSkill (pages or sentences), MergeSkill and AzureOpenAIEmbeddingSkill (local embedding model) with index projections; every other skill type (OCR, entity, language, image, custom WebApi) fails the indexer naming the skill. No knowledge store.

azure.aisearch.wire.title: Native data-plane wire for the azure-search-documents clients (SearchIndexClient, SearchClient, SearchIndexerClient)
limitations: The appliance serves the OData wire the unmodified clients send (azure-search-documents 12.1.0): `indexes('x')`, `docs/search.post.search|suggest|autocomplete`, `docs/search.index`, `docs('key')`, `docs/$count`, `search.stats`, datasources/indexers (`search.run|status|reset`)/skillsets/synonymmaps/aliases, `servicestats`. Three ways to reach a service: the root endpoint (the only search service in the space answers), `<host>/azure-data/search/<service>`, or a `<service>.search.*` Host header. api-key: admin keys do everything, query keys only read documents and run queries (403 otherwise); a bearer token is accepted. The service resolves from the ARM Search records of the Azure space, whose advertised `properties.endpoint` (`https://<name>.search.windows.net/`) is not resolvable locally: use one of the three forms. Offline appliance only: the Nano shared router does not route this wire yet. Indexer triggering from Event Grid is separate.

azure.aisearch.indexer.blob-fill.title: Indexer over an Azure Blob data source (account connection string or UseDevelopmentStorage=true) fills the target index; re-run picks up new blobs
limitations: Proven with blobs uploaded by azure-storage-blob and the service/admin key from azure-mgmt-search, driving the ARM-extension data-plane path; the native SearchIndexerClient wire is the az-ref-ai lane's. Skillset embedding skills need the local model seam (BLOCKED without a model); text/JSON/CSV parsing, field mappings, change tracking and Cosmos/SQL sources are covered by test_azure_search_core.py.

azure.aisearch.iam.title: Access control (IAM) on a search service
limitations: Role assignments, role definitions and Check access are real ARM resources and a real evaluation scoped to this resource id (core/azure_iam_core.py), but the simulator only enforces them when IAM enforcement is switched on for the resource.
